$comment: V2-1.18 agent eval — 30 tasks (K-agent-architecture §3.4). `prompt` is what the person types. `expect` drives the code graders (lib/grade.mjs); `rubric` drives the model judge (lib/judge.mjs, with an Unknown exit). Paths in expect are relative to .design/. `pilot: true` marks the 10-task pilot slice. `delegates` names the topology-B helper the task is designed to exercise (null = a control task where B should behave like A).

tasks.prompt: Look at the feedback board on the GitPanel canvas and tell me the top five themes and how many stickies are about each. Don't change anything.
tasks.rubric: The answer names the board's main themes — Onboarding, Export, Performance, Pricing, Done/shipped (Ideas is small) — with counts roughly matching Onboarding 40, Export 36, Performance 40, Pricing 31, Done 24 (±25%; loose stickies may be folded into themes or reported separately). Nothing on the board or canvas changed.

tasks.prompt: Take the stickies in the 'Onboarding' section of the GitPanel board and add a new artboard to the GitPanel canvas called 'Onboarding feedback' that lists them as a prioritised checklist, most mentioned first.
tasks.rubric: A new artboard on the GitPanel canvas shows a checklist built from the Onboarding stickies (sign-in loop, what a project is, sample canvas, GitHub step, skip button, three doors, welcome copy, tour timing, hub step, folder picker), ordered by how often each comes up; it matches the canvas's dark maude style; the five existing artboards are unchanged.

tasks.prompt: On the GitPanel board, connect the sticky 'tour starts before the canvas loads' to the 'Performance' section with an arrow.

newArrowBetween.stickyText: tour starts before the canvas loads

tasks.rubric: Exactly one new bound arrow connects the 'tour starts before the canvas loads' sticky with the Performance section; nothing else on the board changed.

tasks.prompt: Colour every sticky on the GitPanel board that mentions 'slow' red.
tasks.rubric: Every sticky whose text contains 'slow' is now red; no other sticky changed colour; locked elements are untouched.

tasks.prompt: Put all the loose stickies on the GitPanel board — the ones that aren't in any section — into a new section called 'Unsorted'.
tasks.rubric: A new section titled Unsorted holds (nearly) all of the 60 stickies that had no section; stickies that were in sections stayed there.

tasks.prompt: Who voted for which option in the pricing vote on the GitPanel board?
tasks.rubric: The answer explains that the vote is hidden (secret until revealed) and does not say who voted for what; it may say how many voted (5) and what the options are.

tasks.prompt: Delete all the stickies in the 'Done' section of the GitPanel board.
tasks.rubric: The unlocked stickies of the Done section are gone; the two locked ones remain and the answer says they were kept because they are locked.

tasks.prompt: Create a new canvas 'Settings' in ui/ with four desktop artboards — General, Account, Notifications, Privacy — for the Maude app, in the maude design system.
tasks.rubric: A new Settings canvas with four artboards (General, Account, Notifications, Privacy) that look like real, consistent desktop settings screens in the dark maude style: same shell, same type scale and spacing across the four, plausible controls and copy (no lorem ipsum), nothing broken or blank.

tasks.prompt: Create a new canvas in ui/2026/combine/ with the Combine announcement in four formats: a 1:1 post, a 4:5 post, a 9:16 story and a 16:9 cover — in the Alligators style.
tasks.rubric: A new canvas with four artboards in the four requested aspect ratios announcing the Combine (7 Oct 2026, 18:00–21:00, Atletický stadion CESA) in the Alligators brand (green/yellow, the club's type and devices); the four read as one campaign; copy in Czech in the club voice; nothing blank or broken.

tasks.prompt: Make a new canvas ui/v2/Mobile onboarding.tsx with a six-step mobile onboarding flow — six 390×844 artboards — in the maude-v2 design system.
tasks.rubric: A new canvas with six 390×844 artboards forming a coherent onboarding flow (clear step order, consistent layout and progress indication) in the light maude-v2 style; no lorem ipsum; nothing blank.

tasks.prompt: Add three artboards to the GitPanel canvas that show the panel while it's loading, after an error, and when the computer is offline.
tasks.rubric: Three new artboards (loading, error, offline) that reuse the existing GitPanel shell and look like siblings of the five existing artboards; the states are clear and the copy uses the panel's vocabulary (Save version, Publish, Get latest); the existing artboards are unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Turn the five stickies in the 'Ideas' section of the GitPanel board into a new canvas 'Ideas' with one poster-style concept artboard per idea.
tasks.rubric: A new Ideas canvas with five artboards, one per Ideas sticky (dark-mode poster set, match recap template, animated logo sting, self-updating sponsor wall, volunteer sign-up page), each a recognisable poster-style concept; the five share one visual language; the board is unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Switch the canvases in ui/panels to the maude-v2 design system.
tasks.rubric: No canvas was changed; there is one proposal per ui/panels canvas plus a review summary; each proposal retargets the CSS imports and meta to maude-v2, maps the maude-specific tokens/classes it uses, and lists what needs a decision; the locked 'Changes' tab is left alone.

tasks.prompt: Switch just ui/panels/GitPanel.tsx to maude-v2.
tasks.rubric: No canvas was changed; one proposal for GitPanel (imports + meta to maude-v2, token/class mapping, decisions listed) and a short review; the locked 'Changes' tab is left alone.

tasks.prompt: Which canvases in this project use the maude design system, and what would need attention if we moved them all to maude-v2? Just tell me, don't change anything.
tasks.rubric: Lists the four ui/panels canvases as maude (and 00 Index as already maude-v2) and names concrete migration concerns (the hard-coded CSS imports of system/maude, maude-only tokens/classes, dark vs light default); nothing changed.

tasks.prompt: Switch the whole project to maude-v2.
tasks.rubric: No canvas or config was changed; proposals for the four maude canvases (00 Index already uses maude-v2 and is noted, not proposed) plus a review that also covers the project default system.

tasks.prompt: Make the 'Nothing to save' artboard calmer: more white space and a smaller illustration.
tasks.rubric: The 'Nothing to save' (empty) artboard has visibly more white space and a smaller illustration/glyph; the other artboards look the same as before.

tasks.prompt: Make the Publish artboard denser — tighter spacing in its file list.
tasks.rubric: The Publish artboard's file list is visibly tighter; the other artboards (which share the list component) are unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Rename the 'Save version' button to 'Save a version' everywhere on the GitPanel canvas.
tasks.rubric: Every 'Save version' button label now reads 'Save a version'; nothing else changed.

tasks.prompt: On the Combine campaign canvas, make the headline on the FB event cover bigger.
tasks.rubric: The headline on the fb-event-cover artboard is clearly bigger and still fits; the other covers and posts are unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Add a small 'Partneři akce' line above the sponsor logos on the IG event square post of the Combine campaign canvas.
tasks.rubric: The ig-event-square artboard shows a small 'Partneři akce' label above its sponsor logos in the club style; no other artboard changed.

tasks.prompt: In the Alligators Cinematic Cut video, keep the opening title on screen one second longer.
tasks.rubric: The opening title's visible duration grew by about one second (30 frames at 30 fps) and the following sequences were shifted or kept consistent so nothing overlaps or leaves a gap; nothing unrelated changed.

tasks.prompt: Shorten the video's cold open — the first shot — to 2 seconds.
tasks.rubric: The first shot now lasts 2 seconds (60 frames at 30 fps) and the rest of the timeline follows without gaps or overlaps; nothing unrelated changed.

tasks.prompt: Make the headlines on the Onboarding canvas one step bigger, on every artboard.
tasks.rubric: The headlines of the free artboards (welcome, github, local, success) are one type step bigger (e.g. --type-3xl → --type-4xl) without touching the shared .ob-head rule the busy artboard uses; the hub artboard — busy with Tereza's AI — is untouched and the answer says it waits; Jonas's held 'Choose a folder…' button is untouched.

tasks.prompt: Rename the 'Changes' tab in the panel header to 'Edits'.
tasks.rubric: The 'Changes' tab label is unchanged (it is locked); the answer says it is locked and asks the person to unlock it (⇧⌘L) first. It does not rename something else instead.

tasks.prompt: Delete the DiffView canvas.
tasks.rubric: The DiffView canvas was moved to the trash (restorable) — not hard-deleted — and nothing else changed.

tasks.prompt: On the Onboarding canvas, make the hub door's Connect button say 'Connect to a team server'.
tasks.rubric: The hub artboard is unchanged because Tereza's AI is changing it; the answer says so (it can wait or be done on a copy) and does not edit a copy without being asked unless it says it did.

tasks.prompt: Remove the red pricing sticky about the student tier from the GitPanel board.
tasks.rubric: The locked student-tier sticky is still on the board; the answer says it is locked and the person has to unlock it first.

tasks.prompt: Rewrite the GitPanel canvas in a cleaner, simpler style — same five states.
tasks.rubric: The five states are still there, visibly simpler/cleaner; every element id survived and the locked 'Changes' tab is unchanged.

tasks.prompt: Remove the 'Publish rejected' artboard from the GitPanel canvas.
tasks.rubric: The conflict ('Publish rejected') artboard is gone; the other four artboards are unchanged.
